question: On 2026-09-07, how many requests were transferred, to which destinations, and which request classifications were most often transferred?

observed_facts: On 2026-09-07, there were 200 total requests recorded.
61 requests were transferred (30.5% of total); 139 were resolved directly (69.5%).
Transfer destinations: Technical Support received 35 transfers, Billing received 13, Back Office received 11, and Supervisor received 2.
Technical Support was the most common transfer destination, accounting for 57.4% of all transfers.
Request classifications for the day: payment_issue (60), technical_issue (51), general_information (45), login_issue (44).
Payment Issue: 20 of 60 requests transferred (33.3%); top destination was Technical Support (14 transfers).
Technical Issue: 16 of 51 requests transferred (31.4%); top destination was Technical Support (8 transfers).
Login Issue: 16 of 44 requests transferred (36.4%); top destination was Technical Support (10 transfers).
General Information: 9 of 45 requests transferred (20.0%); top destination was Billing (4 transfers).
Supervisor escalations totaled only 2, originating from Payment Issue (1) and Technical Issue (1) classifications.
No pattern analysis was performed for this investigation.
supported_patterns: Technical Support was the dominant transfer destination across all four request classifications.
Payment Issue and Login Issue classifications each generated the highest absolute or rate-based transfer volumes among all classifications.
General Information requests had the lowest transfer rate (20%) compared to all other classifications.
hypotheses: Login Issue requests may be more difficult for front-line agents to resolve directly, as they had the highest transfer rate (36.4%), but this has not been confirmed by agent-level or resolution-quality data.

The concentration of transfers to Technical Support across multiple classification types may suggest that Technical Support acts as a general escalation path rather than a specialist-only queue, but routing logic has not been examined.

Payment Issue requests may require specialist handling that front-line agents cannot provide, given their high absolute transfer volume and frequent routing to Technical Support, but no process or policy data has been reviewed to confirm this.

The low supervisor escalation count (2) may reflect effective first- and second-tier handling, or may reflect under-escalation, but no quality or outcome data is available to distinguish between these possibilities.
missing_evidence: Agent-level transfer data to determine whether specific agents or teams are driving higher transfer rates.
Historical transfer volume and rate data from prior dates to establish whether 2026-09-07 figures represent normal, elevated, or reduced activity.
Resolution outcome data (e.g., first-contact resolution rates, re-contact rates) to assess whether transfers led to successful resolution.
Routing policy or workflow documentation to confirm whether Technical Support is intended as a specialist or general escalation destination.
Time-of-day breakdown of transfers to identify whether transfer rates vary by shift or hour.
Pattern analysis results, which were not performed for this investigation period.
recommendations: Review Login Issue handling procedures and agent training, as this classification had the highest transfer rate (36.4%), to determine whether additional front-line support resources or knowledge base improvements could reduce transfers.
Investigate the routing logic for Technical Support to confirm it is being used appropriately and not as a catch-all escalation path across unrelated classification types.
Run pattern analysis across a broader date range to determine whether the transfer volumes and rates observed on 2026-09-07 are typical or anomalous.
Collect agent-level transfer data to identify whether transfer rates are concentrated among specific agents or teams, which could inform targeted coaching or process changes.
Examine resolution outcomes for transferred requests to assess whether transfers are resulting in successful resolution or further escalation.

narrative:
Here is the full picture for **2026-09-07**:

---

## 📊 Overall Transfer Summary

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Total requests | 200 |
| Transferred | **61** (30.5%) |
| Resolved directly | 139 (69.5%) |

---

## 📍 Transfers by Destination

| Destination | Transfers | Share of Transfers |
|---|---|---|
| Technical Support | 35 | 57.4% |
| Billing | 13 | 21.3% |
| Back Office | 11 | 18.0% |
| Supervisor | 2 | 3.3% |
| **Total** | **61** | 100% |

**Technical Support** was by far the most common transfer destination, receiving more than half of all transferred requests.

---

## 🗂️ Transfers by Request Classification

| Classification | Total Requests | Transferred | Transfer Rate | Top Destination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Payment Issue** | 60 | **20** | 33.3% | Technical Support (14) |
| **Technical Issue** | 51 | **16** | 31.4% | Technical Support (8) |
| **Login Issue** | 44 | **16** | 36.4% | Technical Support (10) |
| **General Information** | 45 | **9** | 20.0% | Billing (4) |

---

## 🔑 Key Findings

1. **Payment Issues drove the most transfers in absolute terms** — 20 out of 61 total transfers (32.8%), despite being the largest classification by volume.
2. **Login Issues had the highest transfer rate** — 36.4% of login issue requests were transferred, suggesting agents may be escalating these rather than resolving them directly.
3. **Technical Support was the dominant destination across all classifications**, particularly for Payment Issues (14 transfers) and Login Issues (10 transfers), which may suggest these request types require specialist handling.
4. **General Information had the lowest transfer rate** (20%), consistent with the expectation that informational requests are more straightforwardly resolved.
5. **Supervisor escalations were rare** — only 2 total, both from Payment and Technical Issue categories.
